Vectors_Act1_WhatAVectorIs.text: The only room in the chapter whose floor already matches its lesson one to one â€” a where, a which-way, a how-far and a how-far refused, and deliberately no arithmetic; leave the four stations exactly as they stand.

VFM_02_Operations.text: The bench. Twenty-seven instruments and not one caption: every operation here is said again in the captioned room next door, at walk-in scale.

Vectors_Act2_VectorArithmetic.text: The tutorial. Eight caption panels down column 9 and one rung beside each: add, subtract, scale, dot, project, cross, and the two laser exhibits at the door.

The tutorial hall for rung 2, and the room where the chapter's two-scale rhythm is said inside a single space: six operations, each once in your hand and once at the size of a room, in the order the eight caption panels stand down the centre aisle. Ten rungs on the thread, hand then room at each of the four paired stations; the two laser exhibits at the door stay in the room as a third scale met after the closing line, not as a lesson. The bench next door holds the same instruments and defers all of them here, so this is where an operation is actually taught.

VFM_05_Launch.text: Thirty-one placements and the room says throw sixteen ways, so the tutorial is F=ma, then the net force, then the arc composed and decomposed, then you as the projectile, then many bodies, then the census that shows all four launchers running one equation; friction_ramp is the one artifact here that would be better MOVED than demoted â€” it belongs beside wedge_slide in Act4a.

Vectors_Act3_FieldsAndMotion.text: One primary compares two receiver rules in the same field. VectorMotion remains a supporting exhibit after its primary encounter in the previous hall. All 13 artifact identities remain; previous prose and roles are backed up in doc/space/field-receivers-2026-09-11/before.

Vectors_Act4a_KineticForces.text: The park is already a clean five-rung tutorial â€” work, drag, turn, fall, slope â€” and the only change is force_pad, which keeps its floor beat and its place at the park's midpoint but stops carrying a lesson launch already owns; the two category heroes stay exactly where they are, doing a hero's job of setting the register before the beats speak.

Vectors_Act4b_Oscillation.text: FLAG for Palle: the room's law is F = -kx and the floor delivers spring_tower LAST â€” spawn is south, the tower is north â€” so the room's own tutorial.md opens on the artifact the walk closes on; swapping spawn and teleporter is the one map change that would make this room's order correct, and it is a decision for you, not for this pass.

VFM_07_Gravity.text: The two primary experiments now lead the walk, at (11,8) and (11,24). All nine supporting artifacts follow in their original relative arrangement.

The new primaries share a softened gravity law. Supporting graph layout and other legacy solvers use their own rules; do not present them as identical implementations. Earlier notes are preserved in the revision record.

VFM_09_Legs.text: The seven original walkers remain as a comparison family. The physical support table and the four-leg walker anchor the book: support geometry, actual contact, and procedural stepping are distinct. Earlier leg-count claims and placements are archived in the revision record.

VFM_08_Arena.text: A scoped creature encounter precedes the retained collision-carts comparison. Other Arena artifacts remain supporting encounters with their own rules. The previous exam/primary count note is archived in the before record.

Vectors_Act5_ForceAsPlace.text: Aim the machine, observe the probe, then enter the field. The retained plank makes a second crossing available. Desktop carry and landing are verified; headset visit remains open. The former forced-crossing note is archived in the before record.

VFM_03_Motion.text: The motion bench. Its own intent names the stations: the eight-metre bouncing-ball chamber anchors it, the friction threshold and the normal force stand together, and the collision crasher prowls the far corner behind a warning.

Array.text: THE OVERTURE (Palle, 2026-09-07). This hall keeps row_3_x, column_3_z, grid_2d_4x4 and grid_3d_4x4x4 even though each now has its own room in the revived array_tutorial ladder. That is the point: you see the whole ladder standing at once before you climb it, and the seven rooms after take one rung each. The duplication is the argument, not debt from the 2026-08-24 fold.

WaveFunctions_Effect_Sound.text: The book follows DualBallFMController: hold one note, change one modulator direction, compare, then inspect the phase-modulation expression. The surrounding racks remain further explorations. The scope selects two carrier periods and rescales its lanes; a visible trace and a heard note preserve different evidence. Claude built and repaired the encounter; Astra independently reviewed it on 12 September with 100 passing desktop checks. Listening and headset review remain open.

FormFinding_Descent.text: Begin with the controlled landscape. Retain the five earlier exhibits as comparisons with distinct dynamics. Small slope, frame exit and budget exhaustion are separate endings; headset walkthrough pending.
